```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 9, fig.height = 5)
```

# 1. Setup

All functions live in `technical_analysis_functions.R`. Sourcing it loads the
required packages (**quantmod**, **TTR**, **xts**, **zoo**) and defines the
utilities used below.

```{r load-functions}
source("technical_analysis_functions.R")
sapply(required_packages, function(p) as.character(packageVersion(p)))
```

# 2. Portfolio Configuration

The portfolio is defined in `portfolio.txt`, one ticker per line.

```{r portfolio}
portfolio <- read_portfolio("portfolio.txt")
portfolio
```

# 3. Import Stock Data

`load_stock_data()` reads `portfolio.txt` and downloads one year of daily
prices from Yahoo Finance with `quantmod::getSymbols()`. Each stock is stored as
a **separate data frame** inside a named list.

```{r import}
stocks <- load_stock_data("portfolio.txt",
                          from = Sys.Date() - 365, to = Sys.Date())
names(stocks)
sapply(stocks, nrow)
str(stocks$AAPL)
```

# 4. Display the Imported Data

## 4.1 First and last rows of each stock

```{r display-data}
for (s in stocks) display_stock_data(s, n = 5)
```

## 4.2 Quote summary (Yahoo Finance style)

```{r quote-summary}
quotes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stocks, display_quote_summary))
knitr::kable(quotes, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrrrr",
             caption = "Latest trading day for each stock")
```

# 5. Basic Statistics

`calculate_statistics()` takes one stock data frame and returns a list with a
summary row (mean, median, mode, standard deviation, min, max) and a data frame
of 20- and 50-day simple moving averages (`TTR::SMA`).
`calculate_portfolio_statistics()` applies it to every stock.

> **Mode note:** closing prices are continuous, so they are rounded to the nearest
> dollar before the most frequent value is found.

```{r statistics}
stats <- calculate_portfolio_statistics(stocks)

knitr::kable(stats$summary[, c("Symbol", "Days", "Mean", "Median", "Mode",
                               "Std_Dev", "Min", "Max")],
             row.names = FALSE, caption = "Closing-price statistics (1 year)")

knitr::kable(stats$summary[, c("Symbol", "Last_Close", "Last_SMA_20",
                               "Last_SMA_50", "Avg_Volume")],
             row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Latest close vs. moving averages")
```

## 5.1 Moving averages (last 5 days, AAPL)

```{r ma-table}
tail(stats$by_stock$AAPL$moving_average, 5)
```

## 5.2 Verification

The statistics are cross-checked against base R `summary()` for one stock.

```{r verify}
summary(stocks$AAPL$Close)
stopifnot(
  all.equal(round(mean(stocks$AAPL$Close), 2), stats$summary["AAPL", "Mean"]),
  all.equal(round(median(stocks$AAPL$Close), 2), stats$summary["AAPL", "Median"])
)
"Mean and median match base R"
```

# 6. Visualizations

## 6.1 Portfolio performance

```{r normalized}
plot_normalized_performance(stocks)
```

## 6.2 Close price with moving averages

```{r ma-plots, fig.height = 4}
for (s in names(stocks)) plot_moving_averages(stats$by_stock[[s]]$moving_average, s)
```

## 6.3 Candlestick charts with volume (quantmod)

```{r candlesticks, fig.height = 6}
for (s in stocks) plot_stock_chart(s)
```

## 6.4 Price distribution

```{r boxplot}
closes <- do.call(rbind, lapply(stocks, `[`, c("Symbol", "Close")))
boxplot(Close ~ Symbol, data = closes, col = "lightblue",
        main = "Distribution of closing prices", ylab = "Price (USD)")
```
